title: Tide and Summer
premise: Marine biologist Isandro Eastwick has spent ten years on a quiet Gulf-coast island, counting sea turtles and keeping her past sealed in the drawer where she hid it. When a hurricane-damaged post office releases an undelivered letter postmarked eleven years ago—a confession she wrote to her dying mother about the hit-and-run that killed her sister—she learns the driver was never a stranger: it was Theo Vance, the boy she loved and once protected with silence. As Isandro finally prepares to speak, she discovers Theo has returned to the island as the new coastal development director, and his marina project will destroy the very nesting beach she's fought to protect. Torn between loyalty to the man who became her refuge and the truth she owes her sister, Isandro must choose between justice outside the law and love inside it; in the end she testifies, Theo confesses and accepts his sentence, and years later they meet again on the restored beach—not to resume what was, but to begin something honest.
about_author: Jude Delacroix is the pen name of a former Gulf Coast fisheries observer who traded tide charts for manuscripts after one too many storms. She writes slow-burn romances about people who mistake silence for safety.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Opening on nesting season, we meet her meticulous routines, her turtle counts, and her deliberate smallness of life. A hatchling release scene shows her tenderness and her avoidance. Emotional beat: contentment revealed as armor.

chapters.title: Waterlogged
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Post-hurricane cleanup floods the old post office; salvaged mail is distributed, including a yellowed envelope addressed to her late mother—in Isandro's own handwriting, never sent. She can't open it. Beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, young Isandro's POV. The night of the accident: rain, headlights, her sister Lark's death, and the promise she made to someone in the dark. Ends before naming who stood beside her. Beat: guilt as a shared secret.

chapters.title: What the Letter Says
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Alone at dawn, she reads her own words: a confession that she saw the driver's face and said nothing. The letter names no one—but she knows. Beat: the past stops being past.

chapters.title: The New Man at the Hearing
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At a county zoning meeting over the proposed Vance Point Marina, the developer's representative turns out to be Theo Vance—the boy from that night, back after a decade away. Their eyes meet. Beat: shock braided with old longing.

chapters.title: Small Talk, Large Silences
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo recognizes Isandro instantly and engineers a 'chance' meeting at the marine station. He is charming, careful, and hiding how much he remembers. Beat: two liars performing normalcy.

chapters.title: Nesting Grounds
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced collaboration: the marina permits require her environmental survey. Walking the beach together, old intimacy flickers under professional courtesy. Beat: attraction as danger.

chapters.title: Lark's Room
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She visits her father, whose dementia blurs past and present; he asks when Lark is coming home. Isandro almost tells him everything and instead lies gently. Beat: the cost of protection.

chapters.title: The Witness Nobody Called
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Flashback: the aftermath—his father's lawyers, the cover-up, the hush money, and why he let Isandro take the blame for silence. Beat: sympathy built on complicity.

chapters.title: Tide Charts and Threats
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Her survey confirms the marina would destroy the primary nesting beach. Anonymous pressure arrives—an offer to fund her station if her report softens. Beat: justice and survival start pulling apart.

chapters.title: The Sentence Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She writes and burns three drafts of a confrontation. Her colleague Marisol pushes her: 'You've been mid-sentence for ten years.' Beat: resolve kindling.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo discovers his own company buried the original accident file—and that his father knew Isandro witnessed everything. He realizes returning wasn't coincidence he chose; it was a debt he fled. Beat: the hunter becomes the haunted.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Tropical storm Ophelia turns toward the island; evacuation orders split the team. Theo shows up at her door soaked, saying 'We need to talk about Lark.' Beat: the sentence finally spoken—he says it first.

chapters.title: What We Buried
chapters.summary: Both POVs interleaved. The full truth surfaces between them: he was driving, she covered because she loved him, both were children failed by adults. Rage, grief, and unbearable tenderness collide. Beat: catharsis without absolution.

chapters.title: The Deal on the Table
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Theo offers to withdraw the marina and turn himself in—if she'll wait for him. Her father's health fails; the statute of moral excuses thins. Beat: love offered as another reason to stay silent.

chapters.title: Hatchlings in the Rain
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. During the storm, she rescues a washed-out nest through the night, Theo beside her without being asked. Wordless teamwork becomes the truest conversation they've had. Beat: intimacy rebuilt on shared labor, not secrets.

chapters.title: Lark's Voice
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Sorting her mother's things, she finds Lark's journal—the sister dreamed of being a lawyer, of 'making the law work for girls like us.' Isandro understands silence betrayed more than memory. Beat: the dead get a vote.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, then Theo's. Climax part one: at the reopened inquest, Isandro gives the statement rehearsed for a decade. Theo stands and corroborates before she finishes, confessing fully. Beat: the sentence, finally completed.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The plea, the sentencing, the town's divided reaction; her father, lucid for one hour, tells her Lark would be proud. Theo, from custody, sends no letters—respecting her at last. Beat: grief with clean edges.

chapters.title: The Beach Wins
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. With the marina dead, the county designates the shore a protected reserve bearing Lark's name. Isandro publishes her survey under her full name for the first time. Beat: visibility chosen.

chapters.title: Three Summers Later
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Released, Theo returns not to reclaim but to ask permission—to volunteer, to be accountable, to earn nothing guaranteed. Isandro sets terms: truth first, always. Beat: hope disciplined by honesty.

chapters.title: Tide and Summer
chapters.summary: Shared closing POV. On the beach at the season's first hatchling release, they walk the tideline together—separate footprints, same direction. Isandro counts turtles; for once, she also counts herself. Beat: love as a thing renewed daily, not owed.
